title: ControlFusion: A Controllable Image Fusion Network with Language-Vision De

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 5.2, paragraph 'Comparison with Pre-enhancement' and Table 2
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The authors state: 'our approach uniquely includes pre-enhancement by several SOTA image restoration algorithms tailored to each degradation type. Competing fusion methods are evaluated on raw degraded inputs without pre-enhancement steps, introducing an imbalance that favors our results.' This makes the comparison in Table 2 unfair and invalid; the claimed superiority of ControlFusion is not supported by a controlled experiment.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3, when introducing depth estimation for weather-related distortions
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text says 'd(x) refers to the scene depth, estimated by DepthAnything-V2 [40]'. Reference [40] is 'Restormer: Efficient transformer for high-resolution image restoration' (Zamir et al., CVPR 2022), which is unrelated to DepthAnything-V2. This is a misattribution of a prior work.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 5.3, Table 4 and the accompanying 'Computational Efficiency' discussion
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The table lists separate restoration and fusion costs but does not provide the total cost (parameters, FLOPs, time) for two-stage baselines (restoration + fusion) that are compared against the unified ControlFusion. The claim that 'the efficiency advantages of our unified model become evident' when the two-stage overhead is considered is not quantitatively supported by the table, making the efficiency comparison incomplete and potentially misleading.
